title: Protocol SDK and conformance kit
scope: A golden-fixtures conformance runner: one shared canonical wire-vector file that both the Rust and TypeScript conformance tests load and must reproduce byte-identically. This is the mechanism a client port passes conformance against (reproduce every expected_hex). Predecessor to the platform-port stories.
guarantee: Both languages encode the SAME vectors from the SAME shared file and are asserted byte-identical, so any Rust/TS divergence -- or a future client port that mis-encodes -- fails the conformance test. The kit is extensible: additional formats (cursor/clipboard, more media descriptors) fold into the same fixtures file with a matching case in each runner.

gates.cargo_clippy_common: exit 0 (-D warnings, includes the integration test)

notes: The versioned wire contracts themselves (desktop_control, media_caps) carry stable forward-compatible codes and a downgrade matrix (G017 negotiate), so version support/downgrade is part of the contract the conformance kit locks. Platform-specific bindings/headers are generated from the Rust contract via the existing capi/ts-rs mechanism.
